name: Merv crucible steel
summary: Crucibles from a 9th–10th century workshop at Merv suggest steel was made by melting cast iron together with wrought iron in sealed pots.
description: Workshop crucibles interpreted as evidence for combining cast iron and wrought iron to produce steel.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: One workshop's crucibles showing better blade steel within a continuing Central Asian tradition; scores imply tier 3, well below the reviewed tier 1.
